summary: Configured node1 (OPNsense) to route between two new interfaces (LANA=vtnet1/10.50.10.1 facing node2, LANB=vtnet2/10.50.20.1 facing node3), added firewall pass rules for both, and added a single hybrid-mode outbound SNAT rule (source 10.50.10.0/24, interface opt2/LANB) that translates node2->node3 traffic to node1's LANB address (10.50.20.1) while leaving node3->node2 traffic un-NATed. Verified with real TCP connections in both directions, then completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart/recovery protocol on all three nodes, confirming changed boot identities and full functional recovery of the asymmetric NAT behavior afterward.
actions_performed: Discovered topology: node1 (OPNsense) vtnet0 shares mgmt network with node2/node3 eth0; vtnet1/vtnet2 unconfigured and paired to node2/node3 eth1 respectively
Assigned static IPs 10.50.10.2/24 (node2 eth1) and 10.50.20.2/24 (node3 eth1), added cross routes via node1
Persisted node2/node3 eth1 IP+route via /etc/sysconfig/network-scripts ifcfg/route files (RHEL7 network-scripts)
Edited /conf/config.xml on node1 to add opt1 (LANA, vtnet1, 10.50.10.1/24) and opt2 (LANB, vtnet2, 10.50.20.1/24) interfaces; ran /usr/local/etc/rc.reload_all to apply
Added firewall pass rules for opt1 and opt2 interfaces (default-deny would otherwise block)

Switched outbound NAT to hybrid mode and added an SNAT rule (from 10.50.10.0/24, interface opt2) translating source to node1's LANB address only for LANA->LANB traffic; fixed initial XML field-name bug (source/destination -> from/to) required by SNatRule.php parser

Opened temporary firewalld test ports on node2/node3, ran python TCP client/server tests confirming NAT applies only in the LANA->LANB direction and not the reverse, then removed the temporary ports and test scripts
Captured pre-restart boot identity (kern.boottime on node1, boot_id on node2/node3) and health baselines
Rebooted node2, node3, then node1 one at a time via native reboot commands, polled until each came back, and confirmed changed boot identity for each
Re-verified interfaces, NAT rule, firewall rules and routes survived reboot on all nodes, and re-ran the TCP test end-to-end post-restart to confirm functional recovery of the required NAT behavior
Cleaned up all test scripts, log files, and temporary firewalld port rules

evidence.requirement: node2 (lan-a) -> node3 (lan-b) connection observed by node3 as arriving from a node1 address, not node2's own address
evidence.summary: TCP client on node2 (src 10.50.10.2) connected to node3:5001; node3's peer.log recorded the connecting address as ('10.50.20.1', 3038) -- node1's LANB-facing address, confirmed by the active pf NAT rule 'nat on vtnet2 inet from 10.50.10.0/24 to any -> (vtnet2:0)'

evidence.requirement: node3 (lan-b) -> node2 (lan-a) connection keeps its original source address
evidence.summary: TCP client on node3 connected to node2:5002; node2's peer.log recorded the connecting address as ('10.50.20.2', 38722) -- node3's real, unmodified address
Captured kern.boottime and confirmed pf NAT rule + interface addresses present before restart

evidence.requirement: node1 restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and post-restart recovery
evidence.summary: Reboot command returned before disconnect; kern.boottime changed from 17:16:59 to 17:24:44; post-restart pfctl output shows interfaces, pass rules, and the SNAT rule all intact

evidence.requirement: node1 functional recovery proof (NAT behavior still correct after restart)
evidence.summary: Post-restart TCP test: node2->node3 connection observed by node3 as arriving from 10.50.20.1 (node1's LANB address), confirming the asymmetric NAT still functions after node1's reboot
Captured boot_id and confirmed eth1 static IP and route to 10.50.20.0/24 present before restart
